info.title: A8 API
info.description: REST API for AI agent automation of A8-Reborn platform. Provides blueprint CRUD, device management, deployment control, and VM interaction (touch, swipe, screenshot).

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Paste your API key: `a8k_<prefix>_<secret>`. Also accepts `Authorization: Bearer a8k_...` header.

get.summary: Get blueprint with nodes, pins, edges

get.description: Returns a self-contained, versioned snapshot of the blueprint (nodes → pins, edges) suitable for re-import on another profile. Transient runtime config keys are stripped. Sets `Content-Disposition: attachment`.

post.description: Create a new blueprint from an exported snapshot (the `data` payload returned by the export endpoint). Optionally override the name. Rejects payloads exceeding the node/pin/edge caps (50/500/200) with 422.

get.summary: Get device with tags and widgets

post.description: Toggle the device `locked` flag. A locked device cannot be deleted. Always permitted (no lock gate on this endpoint itself).
Append a widget to the device dashboard. The widget id is server-generated and returned in the response.
Reposition a widget between its siblings. Provide `before` and/or `after` sibling widget ids (at least one required).

get.summary: Find active deployments by device or blueprint
get.description: Look up active deployments (PENDING/DEPLOYING/RUNNING/DEGRADED). Provide `?device=` (matches device name substring or device/room id) and/or `?blueprint=` (matches blueprint name substring). At least one is required. Returns up to 10, newest first.

get.summary: List signal-source nodes in a room
get.description: Discover the signal-source nodes available in a room. Returns `{key, partName, kind}` per node by enumerating the live `${prefix}-signal` parts. Use the returned `key` as `:nodeKey` for the per-node signal routes. `kind` is the wire protocol (`can`/`lin`/`gpio`/`kuksa`), determined per node via a best-effort `describe` RPC — omitted when the source predates the RPC or does not answer in time.

get.description: List available signals on a CAN/LIN/GPIO/KUKSA node with metadata (path, dataType, unit, min/max, allowed/allowedValues, cycleMs, tags, entryType). Read it to drive each signal correctly: stay within the value domain (min/max/allowed/step); CAN `tags.scheduling:cyclic` must be held via /periodic/start (a one-shot actuate is overwritten); GPIO `tags.pinType` dictates the value form (momentary = 1 then 0, slider/multi_position = a domain value); KUKSA `entryType` sensor→publish (actuate false), actuator→actuate=true via a provider. Served by the SignalSource Part over Coolgate.

post.description: Send (actuate) one or more signal values. Accepts a single `{path,value}` or a batch `{signals:[...]}`. CAN: siblings of the same message are packed into one frame (read-modify-write); a "cyclic" signal is overwritten by the bus retransmit — use /periodic/start to hold it. LIN: one-shot frame update, applied at the master's next poll. GPIO: drive per `tags.pinType` (momentary = send 1 then 0). KUKSA: omit/false `actuate` to publish a current value (sensor/state simulation, the usual case); set `actuate=true` only to drive an actuator target through a registered provider. An unknown path → 400. A batch is applied in order and is NOT atomic: on failure the error names the failing index and how many were already applied.

post.description: Start server-side cyclic transmission of a signal value. This is how you HOLD a CAN signal at a steady value — a "cyclic" signal (list → tags.scheduling) is retransmitted by the bus, so a one-shot /actuate is immediately overwritten; start a periodic send, then /periodic/stop when done. Also the only way to meet a keep-alive bus cycle (often ~10ms) that repeated HTTP /actuate cannot. CAN nodes only: LIN/GPIO/KUKSA return 400 (no cyclic-TX concept) — use /actuate instead.

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream of periodic-send status. Emits the current snapshot on connect, then a `{activePaths}` `data:` frame whenever a periodic send starts or stops (the source has no TTL/auto-expiry — status changes only on explicit start/stop); `event: ping` frames are keep-alive. The one-shot `/periodic` route is a single snapshot; this is the live view for a dashboard with several observers. CAN only — LIN/GPIO/KUKSA emit one `{activePaths:[]}` then idle. Content-Type: text/event-stream.

get.description: List the machine-to-machine credentials (Keycloak clients) owned by the authenticated user. Self-service: any authenticated user manages only their own credentials.

post.summary: Create an M2M credential (returns key once)
post.description: Create a new M2M credential and return a single opaque key string `a8k_<base64url(clientId:clientSecret)>`, shown ONCE. Paste it into a client config as `X-API-Key`; the backend exchanges it with Keycloak for a JWT transparently.

key.description: Opaque `a8k_...` key — store securely, shown only once

delete.description: Revoke a credential. Ownership is enforced by the `m2m-<userId>-` clientId prefix — revoking another user's credential returns 403.

post.description: RFC 7662-style introspection of an `a8k_` credential. Requires the cluster bootstrap key (admin); JWT callers receive 403. Used by trusted cluster services (e.g. device-proxy) to validate a forwarded credential without talking to Keycloak directly.
